sense.text:
“For the Lord hath comforted his people, and will have mercy upon his afflicted.” That mercy comes through Christ: him sacrificing his life, dying and resurrecting. That’s the mercy.

We are the afflicted. The affliction was slavery, oppression, colonialism, losing our identity, losing our nationality, losing our culture, losing our heritage, losing our language. Look at what’s going on with our people in the UK, how the white man’s beating the hell out of black men out there on the streets.

“But Zion said, The Lord hath forsaken me, and my Lord hath forgotten me.” Zion is us. This is why we feel like the Lord has forsaken us. We’ve woken up to the truth that we’re Israelites, many of us, thousands upon thousands, yet we still see our brothers and sisters being murdered in the streets, and when we talk to some of our people they ask, ‘What God? God ain’t with us.’ That is what our people say: the Lord has forsaken me, my Lord has forgot me.

Read the names: Tamir Rice, Michael Brown, Sandra Bland, Eric Garner, Alton Sterling, Walter Scott, Oscar Grant, and on and on. These are a lot of names, but this is just the tip of the iceberg; this ain’t everybody they’ve murdered. Not everybody on here was murdered by police, but they were murdered by white folks.

One brother was caught on one of those deer cameras running through the forest. They hunted our brother, and he had no help. They chopped the top of his head off and had the nerve to say animals did that. That is the lies they do. Our sister, a five foot two, 130 pound woman, they said was a danger to the six foot four, 250 pound white cop, and her mother is in torment crying. Kendrick Johnson: they said our young brother did this to himself, that he crawled in there trying to get sneakers and beat himself up real bad like that. You can’t make this stuff up.

With all the murder and corruption, we feel like the Lord has forsaken us, and we say my Lord has forgotten me.

“Can a woman forget her sucking child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb?” God asks the question. “Yea, they may forget”: God says women might forget their kids. “Yet will I not forget thee.” God said, I will never forget the Israelites, I will never forget my people.

We might forget the names. Some of us may have forgot a lot of these names; I might only remember just five of them. But God said he will never forget.

“Behold, I have graven thee upon the palms of my hands; thy walls are continually before me.” God said he graved us on the palms of his hands. So in one hand he got Judah, Benjamin and Levi, Ephraim, Manasseh, all through the 12 tribes graven on his hand.

Christ’s hands were pierced, and all that symbolized was the 12 tribes. When Christ showed Thomas the wounds in his hands, ‘look at my hands’, all that goes back to this verse, how we are graven on the palms of his hands, even when he returns.

So what does that mean? He will always remember the 12 tribes of Israel and never forget us, regardless of all the murder and bloodshed that takes place. He said, ‘I will never leave you or forsake you.’ I will always remember.

precepts.why:
This is the one where we are going to be with Christ in the wilderness and it says we shall look upon him. “And I will pour upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace”, “and they shall look upon me whom they have pierced”: we shall look upon Christ whom they have pierced. “And they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son”: we are going to mourn for him.

The hands that were pierced are the palms the 12 tribes are graven on, and when he returns we will look upon those wounds.

sense.text:
A brother said, what about the Lord’s Prayer? In the Lord’s Prayer he said ‘thy kingdom come, thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven.’ Now we’re going to read his will, the will of the Lord.

“And he spake a parable unto them to this end, that men ought always to pray, and not to faint”. This parable is about prayer: we ought always to pray and never to faint.
“There was in a city a judge”: write this down, this judge represents the Most High, “which feared not God, neither regarded man”.
“And there was a widow in that city”: this widow represents the 12 tribes of Israel, our people. “And she came unto him, saying, Avenge me of mine adversary”: avenge me of my enemy.

“And he would not for a while”. That is why it seemed like the Lord forgot us; that’s why Isaiah said it seemed like the Lord has forsaken us. That is that part of the parable. Many times we pray to the Lord and it seems like he’s not listening. We see all the atrocities that happen to our people, and we pray and pray and pray every day, and it keeps on happening.

Then here it comes: “afterward he said within himself, Though I fear not God, nor regard man”.
“Yet because this widow troubleth me”: this widow, the Israelites, troubleth him with her constant prayers, constant nagging. “I will avenge her, lest by her continual coming she weary me.”

“And the Lord said, Hear what the unjust judge saith.” Here comes the proof of what it means: hear what the Most High said. “And shall not God avenge his own elect, which cry day and night unto him”, for Tamir Rice, Alton Sterling, Eric Garner, Kendrick Johnson, and all the rest.

So when we send up our prayers, we got to ask the Lord: Heavenly Father, send fire on this earth, send judgment on the nations, destroy our enemies, destroy their families, destroy their lives. That’s what Christ said to do. You praying for love and peace; he said pray for vengeance. Pray that everyone that put their hands on our people die a gruesome death. That’s what God said to do, that’s what Jesus Christ said to do. We pray for fire and storm, earthquakes, tornadoes, judgment, judgment, judgment, terrorism in this earth, terrorism in this country.

Believe it or not, that will ease some of the pain that we feel inside. You busy trying to love everybody, but don’t nobody love us. We can’t even get our ruling passed in court to help protect us, our sons and daughters.

“Let me not, I pray you, accept any man’s person, neither let me give flattering titles unto man.” To sum it up simply, a flattering title is an undeserved title.

Wherever you go throughout the earth, mother is a title, father is a title, husband is a title. You have baby mama drama: they call her baby mama because she doesn’t really act or conduct herself as a mother. Baby daddy: he doesn’t really conduct himself as a father, he just had the little thing, he don’t fulfill the role of a father, just like she does not fulfill the role of a mother. Yet on the so-called fake holiday, Mother’s Day, Father’s Day, they get accolades on those phony holidays.

When you start off as a soldier, officer of 10, officer of 20 and 50, there are tests behind those things. It’s a test of knowledge, what you have retained spiritually in your biblical learning, but whether you fulfill it is another story. To say you’re an officer of 10 means you can bring up spiritually and help guide 10 brothers. That is not to be taken lightly. That’s why we frown upon cheating on these exams; there were cheaters in New York, Houston and Atlanta, and we had to change the whole structure.

It’s a dangerous thing. You and your wife are arguing and you seek counsel on how to deal with it, and you got a brother with an undeserved title who don’t know what to say, not spiritually, not scripturally, because he did not get that title because he deserved it. He’s ill-equipped. That was a flattering title: he’s not really an officer of 50, not groomed enough to counsel a marriage. Around New Orleans a brother counseled a marriage and told them they needed to separate for a short time. Years later he counseled them to get divorced. Once they got divorced, a month later that same counselor brother walks in the school with the wife and says, ‘she’s my wife now.’ Like, what the hell. You counseled me to separate from her and you took her from me. Evil.

“For I know not to give flattering titles; in so doing my maker would soon take me away.” God will kill you with a flattering title. He doesn’t play with that.

You read about titles all throughout the Bible. Apostle is a title, disciple is a title. But we must be deserving of these titles. Fulfill your role.

precepts.why:
“I therefore, the prisoner of the Lord, beseech you that ye walk worthy of the vocation wherewith ye are called”. Walk worthy: whatever rank you’re at, walk worthy in it. That is how a title is deserved and not flattering.

It’s not the end, brothers; this is just the beginning. There’s more. The march today went for blocks and blocks, and the captain said this ain’t nothing compared to what the Bible says is going to happen. We are still like a drop in the bucket, a drop in the ocean. But it’s mighty, it’s magnanimous, we love it, it boosts our spirit.

sense.text:
Watch these titles. “And he gave some, apostles”. In the New Testament an apostle is someone who is sent on a mission as a representative of the one who sent them and has the authority to speak for them. The word comes from the Greek apostolos. Apostle is sometimes confused with disciple, but they are not the same. A disciple is a student or learner devoted to learning from Jesus: everybody in this room, we’re all disciples. An apostle is a messenger, one who is sent, and believe it or not, we’re sending some of you brothers out. Walk worthy of the vocation wherewith you are called.

“And some, prophets”. Prophets can have different roles. Teaching prophets teach truth and interpret the word of God. Revelatory prophets receive revelations and directions from the Lord for our benefit. Prophets can prophesy about the future, but that is not their primary function. Many times we think a prophet just prophesies about the future and that’s all they do. No, we’re more than that: we teach and we’re revelatory. Prophets were instrumental in guiding the nation of Israel.

“And some, evangelists”: a preacher who travels to spread the gospel and encourage people to repent.

“And some, pastors and teachers”. A pastor and a Bible teacher have different roles, but there is significant overlap between the two, just like with the prophets. A pastor is a spiritual leader who guides and influences the congregation, gives support and advice on spiritual matters, oversees staff and does administrative and community outreach. A lot of you brothers who are over schools, camp leaders, the head of a school, fall into that. Pastoring involves more personal interaction, seeing the practical needs and spiritual struggles of others. A Bible teacher creates an environment where people can learn about God, explains the scriptures, upholds doctrine and equips others to teach, and teaching is primarily public.

“For the perfecting of the saints”: all these gifts in the body are for the perfecting of the saints. Every congregation needs those attributes, men with those qualities. That’s why it’s very foolish when people say, ‘I only listen to this brother, I only like the way this one brother teaches.’ Each brother has these qualities in verse 11 “for the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ”.

“Till we all come in the unity of the faith”. The churches have never taught blacks and Latinos unity; that’s why they’re all divided up with this denomination and that denomination. When do we start applying the unity that the Bible speaks of?

“And of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man”: this unity is meant to build us into that perfect man, “unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ.” We want to meet the stature of the fullness of Christ. So when we send up our prayers, we ask the Lord to make us into the fullness and stature of Christ, and to bring about that unity our people so desperately need.

There are a lot of Israelite camps out there. We call them orphan camps, because there are no father figures in them. Nine out of 10, it’s all young kids; the oldest might be maybe 30. There are no elders that can go back to the old school and say, hey, don’t do that, this is what happened when that was done. They watch YouTube, write the scriptures down and study, and now they’re on the street teaching, but they have no fathers or mothers.

precepts.why:
“Rebuke not an elder, but intreat him as a father; and the younger men as brethren; the elder women as mothers”. Every congregation needs elders, fathers and mothers.

How many of the women in these other schools can say they came from the old school? Hardly none of them. These are children running around with fringes and Bibles: ‘the white man’s the devil, the white man’s the devil’, that’s all they can say. Yeah, and the white man’s the devil can have a lollipop. They’re children, they’re little kids, and we pray for them.

A lot of it comes from being raised by a single mother: you hate male leadership roles. They see older men there and say, no, I don’t want that, I’m not joining IUIC, we going to do our own thing. That is why those camps have no fathers in them.

Here’s another title: “Now then we are ambassadors for Christ”. Men, we are ambassadors for Christ. An ambassador is an apostle.

An ambassador is a person sent as the chief representative of his or her own government in another country. Our government is New Jerusalem; that’s what we represent. An ambassador is an official representative or messenger.

So we groom you brothers to prepare you for God’s mission, not our own mission. We’re grooming you spiritually and mentally so that you would be a good ambassador, a good apostle, a good representative for the Lord. You can’t be looking all crazy, your hair’s everywhere, you got food in your beard. No, you ain’t ready yet.

That’s why we have specialty ranks in IUIC. With some, not all, we see there’s an issue, and we want you to step out on another level of faith and see how you do, so we say just wait. Some of you don’t know how to groom yourself; you got the scriptural understanding, but there’s something in your personality that, if we sent you somewhere, you might mess things up. So we say not yet, he’s not at that Captain level yet. We send you out with senior men, with the captains or the deacons, and we ask how did this brother do, and we want the report on you. It’s no slight; it’s just a waiting game. Be patient.

sense.text:
“I have set watchmen upon thy walls, O Jerusalem”: the watchmen is you and me. We are the watchmen upon the walls of Jerusalem, “which shall never hold their peace day nor night”. That goes right back to Luke 18: keep teaching, keep praying day and night. This is why we have classes seven days a week, three times a day, and Clubhouse going on now. The word must continuously keep going; we must push this truth. Y’all are fulfilling Bible prophecy.

“Ye that make mention of the Lord, keep not silence”: the Bible says keep not silence.

“And give him no rest”: give God no rest, like the widow woman. It’s saying the same thing: pray and teach, pray and teach, give him no rest, “till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth.”

Jerusalem is not a praise in the earth today. Jerusalem over there in the land of Israel is a dung hill today. It’s garbage; I’ve been there, I’ve seen it, it’s a desert, a wasteland. It is not a praise in the earth, and those are not the people of the book.

Leaders, whether apostles, evangelists or ambassadors, have to demonstrate strong leadership, and that includes the ability to inspire and motivate others. Some teach like dead fish, with the glasses at the tip of the nose: ain’t no fire there, and nobody repents behind that. People read spirits; they can tell when a man doesn’t believe what he is saying. And never think you know everything. There is always somebody better you can learn from, and we glean from those who taught us.

“When they saw the boldness of Peter and John”: Peter and John had the spirit to inspire and motivate the crowd, to motivate Israel to repent, and the people saw that on them.

“And perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men”: they said these guys don’t go into the Greek and the Latin. Paul did go into the Greek and the Latin; Peter and them didn’t. Peter just taught. Yet “they marvelled; and they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus.”

That is the same thing they say about all of us: these guys didn’t go to theology school, but they know this, they know that, and look how they can inspire and motivate the masses of people. That is the Holy Spirit. So we have to keep learning, have the ability to inspire and motivate, make difficult decisions when necessary, at a camp or at the head of a school, and represent our nation with integrity and professionalism, both the inner and the outer man.

A lot of brothers want the position of a leader but lack the experience of being a follower. That’s not how God works: you always start by following, then you work into your leadership. Joshua didn’t just pop up and become a leader, he followed Moses. Peter didn’t just pop up and become a leader, he followed Christ. There are levels of discipleship, and good leadership first begins as a good student. We always read this, but it can never be read enough.

“My son, if thou wilt, thou shalt be taught”: you have to have a willing mind; you have to want to be taught. So why travel all this way and linger in the hall, in security or with the medics, and not be in here learning?

“And if thou wilt apply thy mind, thou shalt be prudent”: this is why some men excel others, even though they may have less time than you. A brother can be around five years and we barely know his name or see him, while a brother who came in one or two years ago is always around asking what this scripture means, what that means. That brother will zip by you, and then you’re mad at us because we exalted him; but bro, we don’t really know you, you stay way back there. At the campfire at Tabernacles, with all the seats empty up front, one brother still sits way back in the nosebleed section, and he has been with us almost eight years.

That is why it behooves all of us in leadership positions to pray for laborers. Everybody in here is not a laborer; you might take up a seat. You might be very busy and still not be productive. There is a difference between being busy and being productive.

“Stand in the multitude of the elders; and cleave unto him that is wise.” That’s what we did coming up: any time leadership was around, we were there, sitting right there. Sit on the floor if you have to. Don’t sit in the back where you can’t hear and then have to ask somebody else what he said; hear it for yourself.
“Let not the parables of understanding escape thee”: ask what a parable means, what this means, what that means.

“If thou seest a man of understanding, get thee betimes unto him, and let thy foot wear the steps of his door.” Sometimes leadership was busy being productive, and when we asked a question they said, I’ll get back to you on that. We didn’t stress or lose our minds because the question wasn’t answered right then; we waited. You have to have patience, because the waters of learning are rising.

“Let thy mind be upon the ordinances of the Lord and meditate continually in his commandments: he shall establish thine heart.” The last part, the wisdom given at thine own desire, comes with studying, praying and applying. That’s getting wisdom at your own desire.
“For the body is not one member, but many.” When people say I’m going to do my own thing, they don’t understand the Bible. One word sums up this verse: unity, working together, keeping together.

“If the foot shall say, Because I am not the hand, I am not of the body; is it therefore not of the body?” The foot is very important. The foot represents the soldiers and the officers of 10, 20 and 50, the test takers. For a body to move and get from point A to point B, it can’t do it without feet. The feet are essential for mobility and movement, and just like at the march today, you men are very essential to this truth. In the body of Christ, members who serve in humble or less visible roles are like the feet: they provide support and stability and enable the entire body to move forward in unity. Without the soldiers and the officers of 10, 20 and 50, we really ain’t going nowhere.

So the foot cannot be envious of the hand. The hands are the specialty ranks and the captains: the movers, the shakers and the producers of the nation, men that can lead men and take a city. We have no fear sending a captain to go take a city: Captain Matthew we’re sending to Grenada for three months, another captain to Jamaica for three months. This is war. People follow a captain not only because he has the love of the congregation but because the captains are scripturally sound. They still have questions, but they’re sound; you’re not going to roll up on them with a Jehovah’s Witness question and confound them.

“If the foot shall say, Because I am not the hand”: hands are used for action, work and service. That is why the hands are the captains, and why we hope to make the brothers in specialty rank captains in time; we see good qualities there, but something else might still be missing. Members who actively serve and work to meet the needs of others in the church are likened to the hands: they carry out tasks, offer assistance and demonstrate love through their actions.

“And if the ear shall say, Because I am not the eye, I am not of the body; is it therefore not of the body?” The ears are very important. The ears are the deacons, able to discern, develop and grow leaders. Ears are meant for hearing and listening: members who are attentive and responsive to the needs, struggles and joys of others in the church embody the role of the ears; they listen, empathize and offer support. The deacons must be able to teach, preach and captivate the people. And the mark of any good leader is measured by the men he leads.

“Because I am not the eye”: the eyes are the Bishops of the congregation. They are at eye level; they have the trust and love of the nation, and they have what most people don’t have: longevity, age and experience.

Eyes provide vision and insight. In the body of Christ, members with a clear vision of the church’s mission, values and goals are like the eyes: they guide and inspire others and give the body direction and purpose. We are always talking about being visionaries, but whatever visions we have must coincide with God’s vision, his word. We are not to have visions that contradict or go outside the word of God.

All that we’re reading here is about unity. If we simply practiced this as a race we would be so much better off, but it is so hard and so difficult for us to practice unity. “If the whole body were an eye, where were the hearing?” Everybody cannot be the eyes.

“Where were the smelling?” The nose symbolizes the sense of smell, which helps detect danger or warning signs in the church. Members who have discernment, wisdom and the ability to perceive spiritual matters are like the nose: they give guidance, direction and insight to protect the body from harm. The higher-ranking captains are the nose.

“But now hath God set the members every one of them in the body, as it hath pleased him.” If you’re a soldier, whose pleasure is it to have you as a soldier? It’s the Lord’s. Whether you’re an officer of 10, 20 or 50, a captain, a Bishop or a Deacon, that is where the Lord set you.

So there should be no envy or corruption among us, nobody trying to overthrow somebody. That’s what happened in the book of Numbers with Moses and Korah and On; if they had only understood this. We are trying to instill this in you so you can roll in the spirit and be cohesive, because the communities where we serve observe, listen and watch. If this one doesn’t like that one and this one wants that one’s position, they’re going to see it, the way you saw it in the churches when we came up. It cannot and should not be among us. When you hear brothers speak like that, they’re not in the spirit of Christ; they don’t have the Holy Spirit on them.
“But now are they many members, yet but one body.” We have many members, yet we are all one body.

“And the eye cannot say unto the hand, I have no need of thee”: the Bishops can’t say to the captains, we have no need of you; that would be the stupidest thing ever. “Nor again the head to the feet, I have no need of you”: nor can the head say to the soldiers, we have no need of you.

“Nay, much more those members of the body, which seem to be more feeble”: the ones you think are feeble are necessary. Take your pinky toe off and you have a problem walking. Brothers who are older in age or have a handicap, who may be in the stewardship program, are still very necessary. And your wives are very necessary: who is going to make the food and watch your kids running around? You need those members.

precepts.why:
“And let ours also learn to maintain good works for necessary uses, that they be not unfruitful.” We all have to learn to maintain good works. When you become an officer or a captain, maintain good works; don’t stop doing what you’re doing.

We wish to see how you conduct yourself when you’re demoted. Brothers who pull back from helping the rest of the body because they lost their rank show they were only in it for a position. Nobody ever says, I’m not going to do anything until I get my rank back, but we can tell by your actions where your heart is: you want a flattering title, and you don’t really have love for the people.

On the other side, if you desire to be moved up, operate a rank above where you are. If you’re a soldier, operate as an officer of 10; an officer of 10, as an officer of 20; an officer of 20, as an officer of 50; a 50, as a captain. We want to see how you can move the people. That is what we look for.

“Yet I supposed it necessary to send to you”: Paul sent a man who was “my brother, and companion in labour, and fellowsoldier, but your messenger, and he that ministered to my wants.”

What we’re reading in the Bible we are fulfilling today: we send you men here and there. We start locally, to get a feel for how you conduct yourselves. If you do well locally, we see how you do in the next state; do that well, and we try another country. We don’t plan on making mistakes by sending wrong spirits places, so we take our time.

Even captains have a captain. “To make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings”: the captain of our salvation is Christ.

So we are no longer going to put undeserving men in as captains. In the beginning, because of the lack of help, we made undeserving brothers captains, and we saw they were never able to fit that role; those were the bug-outs during 2018. We are not even promoting boring, unproductive brothers. You know if you’re boring, and you need a circle where brothers can tell you, no bro, that was boring.

Captain Matthew went up teaching in Ghana and came down asking how he did. We told him he was a boring brother and never to teach like that again, and his whole countenance dropped. But the next day he asked to teach first, and fire came from heaven and burned everybody up. That’s what we’re talking about: teach like that from now on.

An example of the ears. “When the number of the disciples was multiplied, there arose a murmuring of the Grecians against the Hebrews, because their widows were neglected in the daily ministration”: they had a widows’ fund where they took care of the widows, but there was a problem there.

“It is not reason that we should leave the word of God, and serve tables”: the apostles said, we can’t deal with this, we need somebody else to deal with it. “Look ye out among you seven men of honest report”: these were the deacons they chose. Look at that part, “full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom, whom we may appoint over this business.”

This is what the choosing of the deacons is based on. “Likewise must the deacons be grave, not doubletongued, not given to much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre; Holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience.”

“And let these also first be proved”: they have to be proven first before you make them a deacon, “then let them use the office of a deacon, being found blameless.”

“Even so must their wives be grave”: they didn’t just look at you, they looked at your wife too. Grave means serious: they have to be serious about God’s truth. “Let the deacons be the husbands of one wife, ruling their children”, and “they that have used the office of a deacon well purchase to themselves a good degree.”

So the deacons must be able to teach, preach and captivate the people. They are the ears of the body.

The mark of any good leader is measured by the men he leads. “A wise judge will instruct his people; and the government of a prudent man is well ordered.” “As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers”, and what the ruler of the city is, “such are all they that dwell therein.”

Just as the apostles were patterned after Christ, that is how it always is: you are patterned after the leadership. Even in your local school, however the head of the school is, we can tell who is under which captains and which deacons by the way you teach and the things you say. That’s not a bad thing; that’s a good thing.

The eyes, the Bishops, have longevity, age and experience. Paul says he “communicated unto them that gospel which I preach among the Gentiles, but privately to them which were of reputation, lest by any means I should run, or had run, in vain.” See that part, “which were of reputation”: they had a reputation from way back. These were not novices; they were not new leaders.

“A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold.” A good name deals with your reputation. A reputation is your name, whether it’s good or bad, but you want a good name, which means a good reputation.

“Paul and Timotheus, the servants of Jesus Christ, to all the saints in Christ Jesus which are at Philippi, with the bishops and deacons”: see that part, the bishops, plural, and deacons. So it’s not going to stop here. That is why a couple of Passovers ago we raised up Deacon Isaac and Deacon Yoshua.

We are still watching the captains to see which ones we can move up: their life, their wife, their family, the way they carry themselves. It isn’t just about me or about these two; more deacons and more Bishops are going to come out of all of you as well.

What the eyes of the body must be. “If a man desire the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work. A bishop then must be blameless, the husband of one wife, vigilant, sober, of good behaviour, given to hospitality, apt to teach; Not given to wine, no striker, not greedy of filthy lucre; but patient, not a brawler, not covetous; One that ruleth well his own house.”

“As a wise masterbuilder, I have laid the foundation, and another buildeth thereon. But let every man take heed how he buildeth thereupon.” All of us in here, from whatever rank we’re at, are learning to become wise master builders, laying the foundation of Christ. “For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ”: Christ must be the foundation; he is the foundation.

“It shall be revealed by fire”: the Most High is going to try whatever you build. “The fire shall try every man’s work of what sort it is”: these are your trials and your temptations. Everybody gets tried, congregations get tried, and your work gets tried, to see how you built upon that foundation.

“If any man’s work shall be burned, he shall suffer loss: but he himself shall be saved; yet so as by fire.” So you have to make sure you’re doing right. You might have a group of men who don’t want to do right, but that will fall on them.

Even Bishops have a Bishop; bishop simply means head or leader. “For ye were as sheep going astray; but are now returned unto the Shepherd and Bishop of your souls.” The Bishop of our souls is Christ. So even Bishops have a Bishop.

sense.text:
“Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ.” All of us are good soldiers of Jesus Christ, from Bishops to soldiers, every last one of us. Paul was a soldier, Peter was a soldier, James was a soldier, John was a soldier. We’re all soldiers.

So we got to understand that hardness will come. I don’t get excited a lot like some brothers, because I see the picture of what’s going to happen, and I know that certain brothers will not endure hardness when it comes. That hardness is persecution, it’s tribulation, even what we went over today. How many people are offended by us just reading all the names of our brothers and sisters that were killed and asking the Lord for vengeance? That sent spiritual shock waves through the internet. People get pissed off by that, black and white, mad at that: these guys no good, you hear what they’re reading the Bible. Persecution will come. Don’t sleep.

“No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life”: don’t get caught up in it. That’s why even when we do certain things we got to make sure we’re not standing up for drug dealers, pimps, prostitutes. Pooky killed half the block, now he get killed: we’re not marching for that. Pooky was a murderer. Pooky murdered half the block. We’ll stand for brothers like Kendrick Johnson; we’re going to check that story out.

Write this down: good leadership is inspiration, not domination. “The princes of the Gentiles exercise dominion over them, and they that are great exercise authority upon them.” That is the way of the Gentiles.

“But it shall not be so among you”: Christ said we should not have dominion among one another. Don’t dominate each other; that type of a spirit should not be among us.

“Whosoever will be great among you, let him be your minister”: there should be nothing that you do that I’m not willing to do. Even the community cleanup: we started off doing a community cleanup back in the day, we did that, so when it was implemented it was based upon things we’ve done. We are ministers to the people.

“Whosoever will be chief among you, let him be your servant: Even as the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.” The chief is the servant, the way Christ came to minister and not to be ministered unto.

Write this down: good leadership is cooperation, not intimidation.

Story time, back at the job. There was this one boss nobody liked, around 9/11, an Esau of course, always yelling at everybody, yelling, yelling. Two cops, Italian boys, got into a fist fight. I thought it was a real fight, but it was a setup. As they started fighting the boss that nobody liked went to jump in, and a lot of people went to jump in and break it up, and they used that: when you’re trying to hit somebody you hit the other person. They beat the crap out of that dude. The boss got knocked, teeth everywhere, and they made like they couldn’t see because it was a melee, but everybody took their frustration out on that boss. I just stood down and got the hell out of there. So we got to learn to rule; we got to learn to have cooperation, not intimidation.

“The fear of the Lord goeth before the obtaining of authority: but roughness and pride is the losing thereof.” We’ve had men we had to take down for roughness and pride. Brothers have abused their authority, and we said no, we got to take this dude down. Having women stand up all day until the last man comes into the school: where you learn that from? That’s insanity.

Write this down: good leadership focuses on self-improvement. If you think you all right, you got a problem, bro. What is there about me that I can improve? Is it the way I dress, the way I look, the way I speak, the way I teach? There’s always room for self-improvement. Even on the job out there, if you want a better job you got to make certain sacrifices to improve yourself to get to where you want to be. If you want to become that entrepreneur, improve yourself; there’s nothing wrong with that.

“And now, brethren, I commend you to God, and to the word of his grace, which is able to build you up.” Brothers, the word of God is able to build us up. We all got shortcomings, and the word of God is the only thing that can build us up. Some of y’all got your face screwed up because a captain is yelling at you, but he’s trying to build you up, make you a better man, a better husband, a better father. It’s not meant to destroy you.

We go to warfare and brothers are passing out because they’re too damn heavy to march three blocks. Everybody okay? I can make it, bro. Seventy feet off the ship he collapsed, timber, boom, and brothers had to help drag this dude back on the ship. We said no, we can’t go through that no more: the nations are watching, that big fat guy right there fell and passed out. You know how embarrassing that is? So now we’re trying to help brothers improve, and some of y’all mad. Women do that: you try to help improve them and they get mad, and some of you brothers are just like that. If your woman says to you, do I look fat in this, you should be able to tell her yes, you do, it’s not bad, I love you, I want you to be healthy, so work on it; that shouldn’t be an insult. That’s exactly right.

So only the Bible can build us up, brothers, the word of God. This is what we got to let our people in the various communities that we serve understand: only the Bible can build up what is lacking, “and to give you an inheritance among all them which are sanctified.”

precepts.why:
“But ye, beloved, building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Ghost.” Notice what it says: building up yourselves. We can give you the tools, but it’s up to you men to build yourselves up, in whatever area you know is lacking, or that your peers, your brothers, can tell you you’re lacking.

Some of you are terrible husbands, and a brother says, hey bro, you treat your wife like a slave, don’t do that. You should listen to the brother, because he’s trying to help you. Some of you get angry at work, come home and take your frustrations out on your baby, and when we try to correct you, you mad at us like we’re your enemy. We’re trying to keep you out of jail, bro, because you will go to jail. Get your thoughts correct. Let these scriptures marinate on your mind, your soul. The word of his grace is able to build you up, but you have to build up yourselves on it.

sense.text:
Write this down: consistency and discipline work together.

“Wherefore the rather, brethren, give diligence to make your calling and election sure.” Give diligence to make your calling and election sure. Why? “For if ye do these things”, you shall never fall. So discipline and consistency work together.

Write this down: leadership builds Brotherhood. Another word for Brotherhood is solidarity, and another word for solidarity is unity.

“Honour all men. Love the brotherhood. Fear God. Honour the king.” So we may honour all men; that’s admirable. But it says love the Brotherhood, and that’s above that. We can honour all men, but we got to love the Brotherhood above everybody else.

precepts.why:
“Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another.” Brotherly love, in honour preferring one another. Preferring one another.

Somebody says, that’s racist. What do you mean that’s racist? We love our race above everybody else. We love our brothers above everybody else. That’s what Christ was teaching Paul to teach, and that’s what he taught. Get mad if you want; you don’t like the verbiage, but that’s what it is. Honour all men, but love the Brotherhood, preferring one another, above everybody else.

“Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!” That word unity: we’ve read it at least five or six times today. In church we never read that word. It’s never expounded upon, it’s never taught or emphasized; we just sing songs and clap our hands. Now they sing songs and clap cheeks. What the hell is going on with that? Damn. Loving the Brotherhood is brethren dwelling together in unity.

“Can two walk together, except they be agreed?” Read on: “Will a lion roar in the forest, when he hath no prey? will a young lion cry out of his den, if he have taken nothing? Can a bird fall in a snare upon the earth, where no gin is for him?”, and came back to verse 3: “Can two walk together, except they be agreed?”

Unity, solidarity, Brotherhood: that’s what it’s talking about. Our people, we’re learning it. But in the community it must be taught, it must be emphasized, because it’s not being taught in school or churches. There’s a breakdown in the family structure because unity is not being taught, love of the Brotherhood is not being taught. And the love of the brother includes your wife too.

“In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men”. So what is most beautiful before God and man? The first thing is “the unity of brethren”. That is the first thing beautiful to God and man. Then “the love of neighbours”: that’s love your neighbour as you love yourself. Then “a man and a wife that agree together.” All those things work hand in hand, and all those three things are not being taught among our people.

Somebody might ask, what is the difference between the unity of brethren and the love of neighbours? As brethren we believe the same. Your neighbour is your race, your people; they might not believe what you believe yet. The unity of brethren is you and me, all of us up in here. The love of neighbours is us loving our people out there. And a man and a wife that agree together. Unity, solidarity.

Leadership is not about you, brothers. It’s about the people, it’s about the camp, it’s about the congregation. Alone, me myself and I can’t do it, but together we can.

sense.text:
Again, this is not about me, it’s not about you, it’s about our people. “Not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith.” We all have the measure of faith, every man up in here, everyone listening, so we should not try to exalt ourselves above each other.

Let me back up on that in case somebody gets the wrong thought: that doesn’t mean there’s not rank, structure and order. To think of yourself more highly is looking down on somebody, belittling, demeaning someone. It’s saying don’t do that.

“For as we have many members in one body, and all members have not the same office”: all of us in here don’t have the same office. I’m not an IT guy. Yes, I yell at it, but they are very necessary; they’re important, I need them, we need them. Even the kitchen department: I’m not the best cook, there’s people that are chefs. We need them; they’re very important. “So we, being many, are one body in Christ, and every one members one of another.”

“Whether prophecy, let us prophesy according to the proportion of faith”. Some of you may only be able to prophesy Deuteronomy 28. That’s fine, that’s good. If that’s all you know, prophesy that, talk about that, and it’s still happening. You say prophecy, that’s history? No: our people are still being sold in Libya, places like that, so it’s still going on. If you can prophesy Daniel 7, prophesy. Everyone has a different measure, but whatever level you’re at, prophesy that.

“Or ministry”, let us wait on our ministry. Sometimes you got to wait, be patient; that’s what patience is about. Whether it’s the Bishop, the deacons or the captains, if they say not yet, just wait, brother, not yet. When we started the records, one of the first groups came in young and did a song talking about when Adam and Eve ate the apple. I called the Deacon: what the hell am I hearing? Stop letting these young men do music; let them wait. They good now, but back then in the beginning they gave us hell with them records. Sit down, no more records for y’all.

“He that teacheth, on teaching”: some of you are good teachers. Sometimes we say wait. But believe it or not, if the Bishops or deacons can’t do a class, a deacon will say, hey bro, can you teach class for me? That’s your opportunity, your time to shine, so when we walk in: who’s that brother teaching right there? He could teach good on the street, but he’s just as good in the classroom. Teaching in the class is not the same as teaching on the street.

“He that exhorteth, on exhortation”: an exhortation is a motivator. Some brothers have a great gift to motivate people; they make you do something you would never do before. They good motivators.

“He that giveth, let him do it with simplicity”: some brothers have that good hospitable spirit. “He that ruleth, with diligence”: rule with diligence, meaning be consistent. “He that sheweth mercy, with cheerfulness”: be happy when you show mercy, when you forgive somebody. When a brother or sister says, you know what, I’m sorry, don’t take that spirit and go, you ain’t serious, you’re not sincere.

“Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another”: we ain’t been taught that. That’s something we got to write down and meditate, meditate, meditate, because that don’t come easy for Negroes and Latinos. At the beginning of the march today there was a group of Negroes on motorcycles that decided, you know what, F y’all, we going to disrupt the beginning of this. It takes a lot of patience; the thought did cross a brother’s mind, but he said no. Be kindly affectioned one to another: if we teach it and we preach it, we got to live it.

“Not slothful in business”: you ain’t slothful when it comes to the white man’s business, but what about God’s business? That’s what it’s talking about. “Fervent in spirit”: be on fire in your spirit; have Holy Ghost fire when you teach, when you preach, when you put your hands to the plow. “Serving the Lord”: that lets you know it’s talking about God’s business.

“Rejoicing in hope; patient in tribulation”: when we going through hard times, let all of us be patient in tribulation. “Continuing instant in prayer”: pray three times a day, evening, morning and noon. It has to become second nature to us, because we’re used to praying once, or some of us only pray when we eat. Damn.

Leadership is not about doing everything yourself; that’s called micromanaging, and that’s a bad quality. The best leaders know they can’t meet their goals alone; they need the right people doing the right things. Leadership means delegating to the right people to get the job done right. That’s why you got officers of 10, over 10 men; officers of 20, over 20 men; officers of 50. Delegate, delegate, delegate. A micromanager says everybody’s a dumb ass, I got to do it myself. No, that’s bad. I refuse to believe that everybody in here is a dumb ass. There’s some good men with good qualities, smarter than us; why else would the Lord bring them in? Some brothers have carpentry skills, some brothers have electrical skills; whatever it is, there’s a right brother for the right job.

“Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory”: vainglory is vanity, me, me, me, me. “In lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves”. That’s why, when men are teaching, I was telling them: let’s stop interrupting the young men that’s teaching; let’s observe them, let’s watch them. One day a deacon was teaching and a brother asked him a question, and he went into deep waters and got lost. He went so deep he looked back at me to pull him out of the waters. I looked the other way: you got this.

We got to learn to esteem one another. We got to see the good qualities in one another. It’s there; with some it’s deep down in there, and you got to learn to pull that thing out.
Leadership is not about demeaning others. “As a mad man who casteth firebrands, arrows, and death”: you got a bow and arrow with fire on it and you just shooting it, shooting it, shooting it.

“So is the man that deceiveth his neighbour”: that dude with the firebrand, the fiery arrow, is like the man that deceives his neighbour, “and saith, Am not I in sport?” I was just joking, bro, I was just joking. No: the things you said were meant to kill me, destroy me. That’s bad leadership, when your goal is to destroy somebody and then you say, oh, I was just joking. You put it out there, and now everybody knows who you was talking about.

Now the topic changes slightly; it’s still the same, but a slight change. “Now when the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard”: the word adversaries means enemies. The enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard “that the children of the captivity builded the temple unto the Lord God of Israel”.

“Let us build with you: for we seek your God, as ye do; and we do sacrifice unto him since the days of Esar–haddon king of Assur”: that was in 2 Kings 17, when the king of Assyria put transplants in our land.

“Ye have nothing to do with us to build an house unto our God”. So the forefathers said no, we don’t need the other races of people to help us; we can do it ourselves: “but we ourselves together will build unto the Lord God of Israel, as king Cyrus the king of Persia hath commanded us.”

“Then the people of the land weakened the hands of the people of Judah, and troubled them in building”. You see the reaction: they got mad. You don’t want to include us? We mad, we’re going to stop you. That was their goal from the beginning: their goal was to infiltrate and disrupt. But the forefathers, Zerubbabel and Joshua, peeped the game and said no, y’all can’t help us.

“And hired counsellors against them, to frustrate their purpose, all the days of Cyrus king of Persia, even until the reign of Darius king of Persia.” They hired counsellors: they hired people to cause problems among the forefathers in the rebuilding of the temple.

precepts.why:
1 Esdras talks about the same history, but words it a little differently. “Then Zorobabel and Jesus and the chief of the families of Israel said unto them, It is not for us and you to build together an house unto the Lord our God. We ourselves alone will build unto the Lord of Israel, according as Cyrus the king of the Persians hath commanded us.”

Now what we just read in Ezra about them hiring counsellors: watch the wording here. “But the heathen of the land lying heavy upon the inhabitants of Judea, and holding them strait, hindered their building; And by their secret plots, and popular persuasions and commotions, they hindered the finishing of the building all the time that king Cyrus lived”. By their secret plots, popular persuasions and commotions. The counsellors hired to frustrate their purpose worked by secret plots, popular persuasions and commotions.

So they were hindering us, and that’s the same thing happening now. Same exact thing.

sense.text:
“Then the prophets, Haggai the prophet, and Zechariah the son of Iddo”: this is where the class is, Zechariah’s leadership. They “prophesied unto the Jews that were in Judah and Jerusalem in the name of the God of Israel”.

It got so bad that Zerubbabel, who was the leader, and Joshua the high priest stopped building. They stopped the building because there were so many problems: the other nations were hiring people against us, all the secret plots, the commotions. So the Lord raised up Zechariah and Haggai and said, prophesy to Zerubbabel and Joshua.

“Then rose up Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua the son of Jozadak, and began to build the house of God which is at Jerusalem”. You know what the prophets did? They exhorted them, they corrected them. They were not trying to take Zerubbabel’s place or Joshua’s place; those men had the position. The prophets fulfilled their role. The Lord said prophesy, exhort them, do the work, and they did it perfectly. They didn’t have to demean them, belittle them, destroy them, because those were the leaders. The leaders got weak, and the men under them encouraged them to do great works.

Notice the prophet again: he wasn’t trying to take the seat. He was happy and content in his position. That is Zechariah’s leadership.

“Ask ye of the Lord rain in the time of the latter rain”. The latter rain comes during the harvest season, the ingathering. Asking of the Lord rain in the time of the latter rain, we’re asking for the Holy Spirit; that’s what he’s saying.

“So the Lord shall make bright clouds, and give them showers of rain, to every one grass in the field”: to every one grass in the field, meaning to every one man in the field.

precepts.why:
Isaiah is saying the same thing. “Yet now hear, O Jacob my servant; and Israel, whom I have chosen: Thus saith the Lord that made thee, and formed thee from the womb, which will help thee; Fear not, O Jacob, my servant; and thou, Jesurun, whom I have chosen.” The Lord is saying fear not, O Jacob; Jesurun whom I have chosen, that’s us.

“For I will pour water upon him that is thirsty, and floods upon the dry ground: I will pour my spirit upon thy seed”: that’s the Holy Spirit, poured upon thy seed, “and my blessing upon thine offspring”. Watch this: “And they shall spring up as among the grass, as willows by the water courses.” He’s comparing us waking up, this Great Awakening, to grass rising in the field.

“One shall say, I am the Lord’s; and another shall call himself by the name of Jacob”: we’re at this point now; some brothers have an alias. “And another shall subscribe with his hand unto the Lord, and surname himself by the name of Israel”: some brothers have officially changed their names altogether. So you got two levels there, but it’s all working together.

“Then shall we know, if we follow on to know the Lord”. “His going forth is prepared as the morning”: as the morning. “And he shall come unto us as the rain”: that’s that Holy Spirit raining down on us, “as the latter and former rain unto the earth”, like the end gathering seasons, the harvest and the ingathering. That’s the rain asked of the Lord in the time of the latter rain.

sense.text:
There’s a whole lot in verse two. “For the idols have spoken vanity”: the idols have spoken vanity, lies. “And the diviners have seen a lie”: the diviners are the ones who speak on behalf of the idol, and they speak lies. “And have told false dreams; they comfort in vain.”

“Therefore they went their way as a flock”: therefore we, the Israelites, went our way as a flock. “They were troubled, because there was no shepherd”: our people are troubled because there’s no shepherd.

That is a major topic today: why black men don’t go to church. Because there’s no real shepherds in the church. You got feminism and homosexuality, the LGBT community, all running through there, so the real men are leaving the Christian church. Black church foolishness, LGBT, feminism: you can’t make this stuff up. This is why people don’t go to church.

precepts.why:
“Therefore hearken not ye to your prophets, nor to your diviners, nor to your dreamers, nor to your enchanters, nor to your sorcerers, which speak unto you, saying, Ye shall not serve the king of Babylon”. So even back then you had the diviners, these sorcerers, saying you didn’t have to serve the king of Babylon.

“For they prophesy a lie unto you”: see that, they prophesy a lie unto you, “to remove you far from your land; and that I should drive you out, and ye should perish.” The diviners of Zechariah 10:2 that have seen a lie are the same kind.

“What profiteth the graven image that the maker thereof hath graven it; the molten image, and a teacher of lies”: a teacher of lies comes with it. Wherever there’s an idol, you always got diviners and sorcerers that speak for these images.

The Statue of Liberty: what that image represents is democracy, all becoming one nation, one people, based upon ‘Christian’ ideals. Caesar. Mount Rushmore: people speak on their behalf on how great the forefathers of the country were, and they all had slaves. Islam, Judaism, Christianity. What comes with all of these idols are teachers of lies, men and women, black and white. Even in Islam, what comes with that dead meteorite, that stone, is a teacher of lies.

Then look at some of the diviners: why every single Christian Bible teacher is misleading you. These are some of the most famous people your mothers and fathers, sisters and brothers relish: teachers of lies, every last one of them. False teachers exposed. In 2022 they had a mass meeting, and one Negro was there, one African was there.

sense.text:
“Mine anger was kindled against the shepherds”: that’s our pastors, these so-called pastors, these reverends. God is angry with them because they’re not doing what God told them to do, to gather the twelve tribes of Israel. They’re so worried about collecting money and donations and lying to the people to get it. “And I punished the goats”, because they were not doing their jobs, just like today.

The march today ruffled some feathers. Pastor Trevor Turner on Facebook had a few words to say about what he saw: ‘We the church should have gained these brothers’, ‘we have not gone after the men’, ‘the difference is they go out and get the people and we just have church inside with the doors closed’, ‘we don’t worry about them until our young men have funerals in our churches’, ‘I also take accountability for not joining a Ministry that would train me to do more’. This is a confession, a Christian confession. All these pastors say this in their head; not among themselves, but secretly, in their own mind. He’s throwing shade at all the other pastors. And that’s tonight’s class, leadership: how to do more, accountability, responsibility.

The whole point is that whole paragraph is an admission to failure. Most of our people saw us out there; they were in awe, inspired, amazed with what they saw, and he said, we’re failing, the church is failing. Only at funerals, or catering to the women, do they do something; outside of that they’re doing nothing. Oakland, California was the revolutionary place that our people believed was extinguished. He thought he extinguished revolution here; he did not. You guys marched through the streets; you are that light our people needed to see, that light that shines in the dark place. Be proud of yourselves. All praise to the Most High.

“Mine anger was kindled against the shepherds”: this is why. Poison in the black church. A popular minister: let’s sell weed in the church; you can’t make this stuff up. Woke and wicked: that’s the Christian church. A famous mega church pastor arrested for sexual assault. A pastor with a sweater and the hair giving very feminine vibes. A pastor has a thought-provoking question: black man, are you stupid? If you follow the pastors, you are.

“For the Lord of hosts hath visited his flock the house of Judah, and hath made them as his goodly horse in the battle”. He made us like a goodly horse in the battle: he made Judah into a mighty tribe.

precepts.why: The shepherds that God’s anger is kindled against: “Yea, they are greedy dogs which can never have enough, and they are shepherds that cannot understand: they all look to their own way, every one for his gain”. All they care about is money.

So we can understand the goats. “And as for you, O my flock, thus saith the Lord God; Behold, I judge between cattle and cattle, between the rams and the he goats.” See that: the Lord separates Israel as rams and goats. The goats are those rebellious ones.

Why the Lord is dealing with Judah first, visiting “his flock the house of Judah”: he “chose the tribe of Judah, the mount Zion which he loved.” See who he chose: Judah, that’s mount Zion. That ain’t saying he don’t love the rest of y’all, but he said he chose Judah. This is why we catch all the hell, because he’s going to give us some blessings.

sense.text: “Out of him came forth the corner”: out of Judah came forth the corner, the chief corner stone. That’s Christ; he’s the king. “Out of him the nail”: out of Judah the nail, in a sure foundation. That’s Christ; he’s the foundation. “Out of him the battle bow”: out of Judah came the battle bow; that’s Judah coming out of there. “Out of him every oppressor together”: every oppressor is going to be destroyed.

precepts.why: Out of him, which is Judah, came forth the corner: “And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone”. Jesus Christ himself, out of Judah, is the chief corner stone.

Out of Judah the nail: “And I will fasten him as a nail in a sure place; and he shall be for a glorious throne to his father’s house.” Now who y’all think that’s talking about? Who’s the king? Christ, because that’s who it’s talking about.

The chapter before explains what that battle bow of Judah is. “Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope”: our brothers and sisters that were murdered, that was killed. The mothers and fathers, sisters and brothers of our people who have been murdered are hoping for a better day. Our job is to tell them to return to the stronghold: turn to the Bible and learn it the correct way. “Even to day do I declare that I will render double unto thee”: God says he’s going to render double unto us.

“When I have bent Judah for me”: God said, I’m going to bend the tribe of Judah. You might see a lot of things happening to Judah; there’s a reason behind it. Judah is rebellious, and God says I’m going to bend Judah to my will, and that’s what you’re seeing right here. A large majority here is Judah. Fill “the bow with Ephraim”: and you Puerto Ricans, you Mexicans, you ain’t getting away either; he said I’m going to make you do my will. “And raised up thy sons”: I’m going to raise up the rest of the Israelites, those Mexicans, those Panamanians, to the twelve tribes of Israel.

“Against thy sons, O Greece”. What Bible are these churches not reading? Right now this is a spiritual warfare: we are against the sons of Greece, we are against Esau, Edom. God is bending us to his will. Why are you always going against the white man? Because the Bible says go against him, that’s why. “And made thee as the sword of a mighty man”: God said he’s going to make us as the sword of a mighty man.

“And the Lord shall be seen over them”: this lets you know the time period. By the time this gets physical, God said I’m going to be seen over my children, my people. So it ain’t right now, but it’s going to come. “And the Lord God shall blow the trumpet, and shall go with whirlwinds of the south”: that’s the chariots, what they call UFOs, UAPs now.

“The Lord of hosts shall defend them”: God said he’s going to defend us. “And they shall devour, and subdue with sling stones”: we’re going to devour the nations and subdue all the nations, starting with Greece. “And they shall drink, and make a noise as through wine”: we’re going to party.

“And the Lord their God shall save them in that day as the flock of his people: for they shall be as the stones of a crown”. We are his jewels, j-e-w-e-l-s; that’s what Jew comes from. “Lifted up as an ensign upon his land. For how great is his goodness, and how great is his beauty!”

sense.text:
“And they shall be as mighty men”: the Israelites shall be as mighty men. There’s going to come a transformation; the Lord is going to give us spiritual power in these days. “Which tread down their enemies in the mire of the streets in the battle”: we’re going to tread down our enemies. “And they shall fight, because the Lord is with them”: we shall fight, because the Lord is with us, and only us.

“And the riders on horses shall be confounded”: the white man is the rider of horses, those white men in the power seat, and they’re going to be confounded. They put Teddy Roosevelt on a horse and put Gad and Judah on the ground. This is just the beginning, brothers.

“And I will strengthen the house of Judah”: the Lord said, don’t worry Judah, you might be weak right now, but I’m going to strengthen you spiritually, mentally and physically. “And I will save the house of Joseph”: don’t think the Lord forgot about you; he didn’t forget about you either. “And I will bring them again to place them; for I have mercy upon them”: the Lord is having mercy upon the twelve tribes of Israel.

“And they shall be as though I had not cast them off”: it’s going to be like the Lord never sent us to America as slavery, like we never went to Haiti as slavery, like we were never conquered by the Conquistadors. It’s going to be like that never ever happened. “For I am the Lord their God, and will hear them.”

“And they of Ephraim shall be like a mighty man”: y’all see that about Ephraim? That’s you Puerto Ricans. Don’t worry, you might be fat, short and stumpy; God said you Puerto Ricans are going to be like mighty men on that day. “And their heart shall rejoice as through wine: yea, their children shall see it, and be glad”: their children are going to see Daddy, see Mommy; they’re going to see that transformation. “Their heart shall rejoice in the Lord.”

precepts.why: The riders on horses: “I have seen servants upon horses”. That servant is that white man; he’s in the power seat, he’s on the horse. “And princes walking as servants upon the earth”: we are the princes walking as servants on the ground. We’re the nothings now, but there’s coming a day, and what we see now is just the beginning.

sense.text: “I will hiss for them”: you know a snake hisses. Hiss has two applications: to call, and to express contempt or scorn. So God’s calling to us and expressing scorn to the other nations. I’m going to hiss for Israel. “And gather them; for I have redeemed them”: Christ ain’t redeeming all people on earth, only Judah and Joseph, Judah and Ephraim. That’s it. “And they shall increase as they have increased.”

“And I will sow them among the people: and they shall remember me in far countries”. This brother’s waking up. Some of us was that simple brother in the crowd saying, what, we’re the Israelites? You’re not dumb, you’re an Israelite. That ‘dumb Puerto Rican’? No, you’re an Israelite. That ‘dumb Mexican’? No, you’re an Israelite.

We shall remember the Lord in far countries. Believe it or not, America’s far from Jerusalem; we’re in a far country. “And they shall live with their children, and turn again.”

“I will bring them again also out of the land of Egypt”: that’s America, with the chariots. “And gather them out of Assyria”: the other lands. “And I will bring them into the land of Gilead and Lebanon; and place shall not be found for them”: there ain’t going to be enough room for us.

precepts.why:
They shall remember me in far countries. “And it shall come to pass, when all these things are come upon thee, the blessing and the curse”: the blessing happened under King David and King Solomon; that happened already. Now we’re under the curses. “And thou shalt call them to mind among all the nations”: you Israelites shall call these things to mind among Haiti, Jamaica, Sudan, Puerto Rico, Mexico, America, Europe, “whither the Lord thy God hath driven thee”.

“And shalt return unto the Lord thy God”: that’s what we’re doing now, we’re returning to the Lord our God. “And shalt obey his voice according to all that I command thee this day, thou and thy children”: you and your children must obey, “with all thine heart, and with all thy soul”.

“That then the Lord thy God will turn thy captivity”: when we do that, when we obey, God said then I shall turn your captivity, “and have compassion upon thee, and will return and gather thee from all the nations”. Don’t worry about the Israelites scattered worldwide that you can’t even find: from there the Lord thy God will gather thee, and from there he will fetch thee. “And the Lord thy God will bring thee into the land which thy fathers possessed”. We’re going back to New Jerusalem.

I’m going to bring you into the land of Gilead, and one tribe is going to take Gilead. “And they of the south shall possess the mount of Esau; and they of the plain the Philistines: and they shall possess the fields of Ephraim, and the fields of Samaria: and Benjamin shall possess Gilead.” So what tribe is going to take Gilead? Benjamin.

Place shall not be found for them, because when we go back to the land it’s not going to be enough room for us; there’s going to be so many of us. What we see here, as great and monumental as this is, is nothing; they ain’t seen nothing yet. “For thy waste and thy desolate places, and the land of thy destruction, shall even now be too narrow by reason of the inhabitants, and they that swallowed thee up shall be far away.”

“The children which thou shalt have, after thou hast lost the other”: two-thirds of our people are going to be lost here in America. Two-thirds got to die; ain’t no damn good. “Shall say again in thine ears, The place is too strait for me”: the place is too small for us, there’s not enough room for the Israelites. “Give place to me that I may dwell”: give me more room.

“Then shalt thou say in thine heart, Who hath begotten me these”: there’s going to be so many Israelites the question is who’s begotten me all these children. We’re going to have so many children, and our people coming from far and distant lands. The party ain’t over yet.

sense.text: “And he shall pass through the sea with affliction”: he is Christ, the King of Kings, Lord of Lords. The seas are the nations, so Christ is going to pass through the nations with affliction. “And shall smite the waves in the sea”: so you know what time it is. This is war; that’s what it’s saying. “And all the deeps of the river shall dry up: and the pride of Assyria shall be brought down”: the pride of this white man in the nation shall be brought down. “And the sceptre of Egypt shall depart away”: the rulership of America shall end.

“And I will strengthen them in the Lord”: the Lord said he’s going to strengthen Jacob, the twelve tribes of Israel. “And they shall walk up and down in his name, saith the Lord”: we’re going to walk up and down in his name, which means we’re going to walk in his statutes.

precepts.why: What does it mean, he shall pass through the sea with affliction? “Woe to the multitude of many people, which make a noise like the noise of the seas; and to the rushing of nations, that make a rushing like the rushing of mighty waters!” “The nations shall rush like the rushing of many waters”: so it’s comparing nations to the seas, the waters. “But God shall rebuke them, and they shall flee far off, and shall be chased as the chaff of the mountains”, “like a rolling thing before the whirlwind.” Now we got the thought: Christ passing through the sea is Christ passing through the nations.

What does it mean, walk up and down in his name? “For I will take you from among the heathen”: heathen means nations. “And gather you out of all countries”: whatever countries our people are in, I’m going to gather you, “and will bring you into your own land.” “Then will I sprinkle clean water upon you, and ye shall be clean: from all your filthiness, and from all your idols, will I cleanse you.”

“A new heart also will I give you”: that’s the spirit of God, the Holy Spirit. “And a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh. And I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes”. So when it says we’re going to walk in the name of the Lord, it means we’re going to walk in his statutes, “and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them.” It’s a living God.
